title: A Modulus Proof of Cannon's Conjecture
main_claim: Every hyperbolic group G with boundary homeomorphic to S^2 acts properly and cocompactly by isometries on H^3, with finite kernel. The proof uses the Bonk–Kleiner/Bourdon–Kleiner criterion, so it suffices to show that the combinatorial 2-modulus M(n) is bounded. The argument is by contradiction, splitting on whether the record values of M(n) grow exponentially or subexponentially.

issues.location: sec 1, Thm 1.? (uniformization) — citation of Bourdon–Kleiner Cor. 3.5 / Bonk–Kleiner Thm 10.4
issues.description: The whole reduction depends on the cited criterion: on an approximately self-similar metric 2-sphere, bounded combinatorial 2-modulus for curves of diameter ≥ d_0 gives a quasisymmetric/quasi-Möbius uniformization. I could not check the exact statement or numbering against the source. The paper's own check of the hypotheses (that its cells form a κ-approximation, that the space is approximately self-similar via the expansion lemma, and that each dyadic scale matches exactly one r_n) looks right.
issues.evidence: The κ-approximation check is correct: the inner balls of radius 2^{-m}/κ < r_n/2 are disjoint, each cell lies in B(q, κ2^{-m}), and each interval (2^{-m}/a, 2^{-m}] contains exactly one r_n.

issues.description: The proof that Stab(b) has at most two accumulation directions is sketchy: the linear growth count and the loxodromic step are only outlined. The conclusion itself is standard (boundary-point stabilizers in hyperbolic groups are virtually cyclic or finite), so nothing downstream is at risk.
issues.evidence: The distinct points q·ξ(n) lie near a segment of ξ of length O(t), which gives #{q: |q| ≤ t} = O(t). That step is fine.

coverage:
I read the full LaTeX: main.tex and sections 01–05. I checked these in detail:
- Expansion formula (base-change identity).
- Rectangle localization and crossing duality via the min-norm vector P (top-to-bottom incidence vectors pair to at least 1 by planar blocking).
- The raw cost function, the two path envelopes F_N and H_N, the oscillation inequality, continuity, and the strict-side connections that make every straddling path meet C_{N,t}.
- Local oscillation and translated-energy bounds, C(g)/M(N).
- Annular estimate: covering of the macroscopic family by σ_q, then integration over t and Cauchy–Schwarz.
- The record inequality M(N−l) ≤ λ^{-l}M(N), equicontinuity, and the measure bound.
- The finite-cell cross-energy (coarea-type) lemma and the continuum-stopping lemma.
- Exponential case: the Hölder magnification bounds (A_k, tail-max indices, δ_k/r_k → ∞), the diagonal approximants with N_j chosen after h_j, the transform comparison, the group-element algebra behind the two-transform identity, the distinct-puncture argument, and the final contradiction.
- Subexponential case: the bad-node children count, and the capacity lemma's exponent arithmetic. Marked measure is O(a^{γD}Δ) against unmarked mass a^{D'}Δ; Σt² ≥ c·a^{-(Q-2)D'}/M(D−D'); (Q−2)β < τ/4. Also the pattern containment constants, the flow inequalities (telescoping, Jensen, giving average bad mass ≤ 1/11), and generation separation.
- Pair section: puncture multiplicity, near-puncture probability (geodesic word split), the far-pair count, the pair alternative, cost-ball containment and scales (R/d)², the multiplicity bound Ca^{Ql}, and the final inequality a^{γDn} ≤ Ck².
- Consequences: Sullivan–Tukia straightening with orientation reversal, and the Agol/Bergeron–Wise corollaries.

As a sanity check, I confirmed that the argument uses both p = 2 criticality (in Cauchy–Schwarz on the energies) and planar topology (in the crossing duality), so it does not obviously prove too much (for example for S^3 boundaries or for p ≠ 2). I did not check the cited external theorems against their sources.
